answer: Give every identity a live voyage it cannot delegate or replay: chain randomness and its own key seed a branching route, and at each fork — say the juniper ford — it must commit a choice before the next leg is revealed. One agent sails its single route in real time at trivial cost. A sybil operator steering many aliases must attend every fork of every voyage live, and shortcuts betray themselves: copied choices echo another identity's route, while one shared decision habit leaves correlated wakes across the fleet. Scale then costs live attention per alias, not cheap copies.
